memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Is this not stored up with me, sealed in my vaults? It is mine to avenge; I will repay. In due time their foot will slip; their day of disaster is near and their doom rushes upon them.' The Lord will vindicate his people and relent concerning his servants when he sees their strength is gone and no one is left, slave or free." — Deut 32:33-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two great truths shine here. First, God says, "It is mine to avenge; I will repay." God sees every wrong, and nothing escapes His notice — it is all "sealed in his vaults." We do not need to take justice into our own hands or be consumed by bitterness over the wrongs done to us, because God is a just judge who will set all things right in due time. Justice belongs to Him, and He will not fail to do right.

This is deeply freeing. When we are wronged, our hearts cry out for justice, and rightly so. But we can entrust that longing to God rather than letting it poison us. Paul quotes this very verse to urge us: "Do not take revenge... for it is written: 'It is mine to avenge; I will repay,' says the Lord" (Rom 12:19). We can release our grievances to a God who sees all and judges perfectly.

The second truth is even more tender: "The Lord will vindicate his people... when he sees their strength is gone." God's compassion moves toward His people precisely when they are at the end of themselves — weak, helpless, with nothing left. He does not wait for us to be strong. He acts when we are weakest.

This is the heart of the gospel. It was "when we were still powerless" that Christ died for us (Rom 5:6). God's mercy meets us at our lowest, when our strength is gone. So entrust your wrongs to the God who repays, and rest in the God who shows compassion when you have nothing left.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I holding onto grievances I need to entrust to God's justice?
2. How does knowing God repays free me from bitterness?
3. How does God's compassion for the weak comfort me at my lowest?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see every wrong and will judge justly, so I release my grievances to You. Thank You that Your compassion meets me when my strength is gone. Thank You that Christ died for me when I was powerless. Amen.
